# Statement ledger

This ledger maps labels of the manuscript on the second moment of the
Stratonovich hyperbolic Anderson model with Gaussian noise fractional in time
to the Lean declarations in this package. Labels and TeX line numbers refer to
the manuscript revision a284420, and labels are written exactly as in its
LaTeX source (for example `P:clock-copy-obstruction`). The ledger was written
and reviewed at the earlier revisions cf979d6, 669ccc9, ba01d98, 3920258 and
975feb3. Revision a284420 makes two mathematical edits that the ledger
follows. (1) In `notes/integrated_spatial_occupation.tex` it adds Lemma
`L:spatial-fourier-bound` (lines 101-164, display `E:spatial-fourier-bound`),
the deterministic bound `A_sp(g) <= 2^(1+alpha) R_alpha b^(alpha/2)` that
`SpatialFourierBound` already proved, and the proof of
`P:spatial-smooth-ratio` (same label and statement) now derives `R_0 < inf`
from it, independently of the finiteness of `S_1^pos`, which it keeps only
for the score inequality. (2) In the main file, `L:damped-homogeneous-norms`
replaces its smoothing and truncation sentence by the multiplier comparison
`E:damped-multiplier-comparison` (a measurable multiplier `m` in `[0,1]`,
nested measurable Laplace domains, positivity after time integration,
scaling asserted only for the original covariance) and its proof by the
corresponding argument. The other changes since 975feb3 are prose and front
matter (title, abstract, preface, a theory-outlook chapter, the reader
edition, Appendices F and G, the list of notation moved to the back).
Every cited label exists exactly once at a284420. Three of them are new at
a284420 and do not exist at 975feb3: `L:spatial-fourier-bound`,
`E:spatial-fourier-bound` and `E:damped-multiplier-comparison`. Every other
cited label exists exactly once, in the same file, at both revisions, and
every such cited lemma, proposition, theorem, equation and section has the
same statement and proof up to whitespace and braces, except
`P:spatial-smooth-ratio` (proof only), `L:damped-homogeneous-norms`
(statement and proof) and the section `S:spatial-occupation-foundation`
(the new lemma). TeX line numbers were moved to a284420 by a line map; each
moved range has the same text at both revisions, and the ranges inside the
two edited passages were mapped to the corresponding new passages by hand
(script checks recorded in `provenance/manuscript-anchor.json`).

## Scope

- The "What it states" column is a faithful paraphrase, sometimes
  shortened. The exact statement is the Lean type in
  `StratonovichHAMAudit/<Module>.lean` (step modules) or
  `StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/<Module>.lean` (library modules: whole results, narrower results, foundations and proof steps);
  `Audit/<module>/` prints the elaborated types.
- The rows cover every public theorem (2050) and 418 definitions whose
  values are stated as facts or that name a manuscript object. The other 89
  public definitions have no rows of their own: 85 (for example `kappa`,
  `delta`, `gauge`, `counts`, `InventoryProduct.partialEval`,
  `OccupationPhysicalClass.volI`, `SpaceTimePositivity.timeMeasure`,
  `TerminalWick.chainMassReal`, `WaveGreenFourier.spherePhi` and
  `OccupationCeilingExact.stepG`) only name quantities or measures used in
  those statements, and four are the instances that make
  `TimeCompletion.Pre` a pre-inner-product space; read their bodies in the
  Lean source or in `Audit/`.
- The `StratonovichHAMAudit` modules check finite, algebraic and scalar
  steps only: exact identities, polynomial and rational certificates,
  real-power bookkeeping, parameter ranges, and a few finite-dimensional
  inner-product and finite-word facts. The exception is `HermiteWordFock`
  (wave L9), which applies `HermiteWord.cut_eq_raw` to the Fock model of
  `FockForm` and so formalizes the special case of `L:finite-word-cutoff`
  with one Gaussian coordinate per color (section "HermiteWordFock (narrower result: `L:finite-word-cutoff` for one Gaussian mode per color and single finite words; finite sums and Bochner integrals not formalized)"); the
  multi-mode case is not formalized.
- Section headings use three categories. (A) "whole result": every
  conclusion of the labelled result is a Lean conclusion under the
  manuscript's hypotheses, possibly with named supplied inputs that are
  disclosed (coverage class same-assumptions or inputs-supplied, conclusion
  full); no other section carries it. (B) "narrower result: ...": a labelled
  result some of whose conclusions are not Lean conclusions, or are proved
  for a modelled object (the class `O` by joint representatives, the rate in
  Rayleigh form, the cost in integral form, an abstract structure standing
  for an object the manuscript constructs, an object that is not constructed)
  whose identification with the manuscript's object is not formalized; the
  heading names what is missing. The one exception is a registered model
  choice (next item): a result whose only modelled object is such a choice
  stays a whole result, and its section names the model.
  Discharging a named input in a completion module does not turn a narrower
  result into a whole one. (C) "foundation: ..." or "proof steps ...": facts
  used by labelled results, not a labelled result themselves; every
  `StratonovichHAMAudit` section except `HermiteWordFock` is of this kind.
  The first cell of an Index row uses the same words.
- Model-choice register. A registered model choice is a documented
  definitional choice that is the standard construction of a manuscript
  object, recorded with the identification that is not formalized. M1 (wave
  L6, Le's decision 4): the wave Green measure in `d = 3` is
  `(s/(4 pi)) map (omega -> s omega) volume.toSphere`, Mathlib's sphere
  measure scaled to the radius-`s` sphere; its identification with the
  surface (Hausdorff or Riemannian) measure of the TeX is not proved. Results
  whose only modelled object is M1 (`L:low-alpha-convolution`,
  `L:phase-contractions`, and the sections `LowAlphaConvolution`,
  `PhaseContractions` and `L9Completed`) are whole results. Missing
  constructions are not model choices: they make a result narrower (for
  example the noise `W` of `P:masked-quotient-obstruction`, the ground
  family of `L:raw-block-indexed-cone`, the chain measures used for
  `L:uniform-series-tail`, the operator paths of `P:radius-mean-anchor`, the
  solution moments of `P:moment-growth-logconvex` and
  `C:static-moment-constant-continuity`).

# Formalization scope

## The paper's argument and where Lean enters

The paper bounds and identifies the growth of `log E[u(t,x)²]` for the
Stratonovich hyperbolic Anderson model. The argument has three layers.

1. **Stochastic and analytic layer.** The chaos expansion, the two-chain
   pairing integrals, Wick pairings (beyond finite families of Gaussian
   values), Gaussian integration (beyond finitely many standard Gaussians),
   imported bounds,
   Laplace transforms and the variational asymptotics. **Not in Lean**,
   except a few slices: the Laplace transforms of the wave kernel and of
   the two-time kernel and the subordination formula (`ClockCopy` and its
   foundation modules), the Gaussian transform of the spectral measure
   (`MaskedSpectralGrowth`), the uniform scalar frequency row
   (`FrequencyRow`), the temporal completion `H_a` (`TimeCompletion`), the
   auxiliary mask norm (`MaskedAuxiliaryNorm`), the Gaussian heat envelope
   of the covariance (`VariationalMean`), a finite Hilbert-valued Bessel
   inequality (`PhaseBessel`), the wave Green measures `G_s` for
   `d = 1, 2, 3` (`WaveGreen`), the spectral identity and positive
   definiteness of `Gamma = delta_0(dx_1) dx_2` (`QuotientObstruction`), a
   finite Gaussian comparison under the positive semidefinite order
   (`GaussianComparison`), the two wave variance directions in spectral
   form (`WaveTwoVariances`), the variational floor and the Rayleigh-form
   rate (`VariationalFloor`, `VariationalRate`), the deterministic Fourier
   bound `L:spatial-fourier-bound` for the smooth spatial ratio and the
   static controls
   (`SpatialFourierBound`, `SpatialSmoothRatio`, `SpatialStaticControls`,
   `SpatialOccupationCompleted`), series types and the continuity of the
   growth types in the temporal exponent (`SeriesType`, `TypeContinuity`),
   the white-noise bound formulas and clock transforms
   (`WhiteRelativeWidth`, `WhiteClockLaplace`), the coefficient bound of
   the interval inventory product (`InventoryProduct`), an abstract `L^2`
   limit of a regularized series under a uniform scaled moment bound
   (`UniformSeriesTail`), the density of test functions in the
   weak-gradient `H^1` (`H1Density`), the physical four-linear extension
   and the spatial energy (`SpatialFourLinear`), the full physical
   occupation class (`OccupationPhysicalClass`; both completed in
   `SpatialOccupationL7Completed`), the scalar and Hilbert-space steps
   of the static interaction and interval coefficient bounds
   (`IntervalScalar`, `IntervalScalarCompleted`), the spectral-mass
   identity `R_Gamma(1) = R_alpha` (`SpectralMassIdentity`), Gaussian
   smoothing as a Fourier multiplier (`DampedMultiplier`), the positivity of
   the space-time occupation form, the deterministic occupation ceiling and
   the spatial bracket (`SpaceTimePositivity`, `OccupationCeilingFinite`,
   `SpatialBracket`, completed in `L8Completed`), the masked rates
   (`RemoveMask`), the finite Wick formula and the terminal-chain Wick
   formula with the chain measures given by their masses (`FiniteWick`,
   `TerminalWick`), an abstract compact Young baseline (`SymplecticFree`)
   and the Cauchy steps of the static phase orders (`StaticPhaseCauchy`),
   the Fourier transforms of the wave Green measures in `d = 1, 2, 3` and
   Archimedes' law for the sphere measure (`WaveGreenFourier`), the low-alpha
   convolution bound and the static contraction bounds
   (`LowAlphaConvolution`, `PhaseContractions`, completed in `L9Completed`),
   the exact occupation constant and ceiling (`RawOccupationEnergy`,
   `OccupationCeilingExact`), the normalized Hermite polynomials and the
   finite Gaussian Fock layer with values in a Hilbert factor
   (`GaussianHermite`, `HermiteFock`) and their consumers `L:fock-form`,
   `L:interval-contractions` and `E:occupied-multiplication` (`FockForm`),
   and the scalar and numerical-range steps of the complex phase bounds
   (`ComplexPhaseScalar`).
2. **Reductions to explicit inequalities.** At many points the analytic
   argument reduces to a finite statement: an exponent range, an exact
   rational or square-root inequality, a polynomial that must stay positive
   on a region, a determinant or matrix inverse, a count of coefficients in
   a finite word, or an integral comparison once integrability is known.
   **These are what Lean checks.**
3. **Assembly** of the main theorems from the layers above. **Not in Lean.**

So each module checks one reduction in layer 2. Its hypotheses state the
facts that layer 1 supplies (for example positivity of a parameter,
integrability of a function, or an inequality proved analytically in the
paper). Its conclusion is the fact that the paper then uses.

Heading categories (the same three are used in the statement ledger and in
every first cell of its Index by label). The ledger Scope keeps the
model-choice register. M1, its only entry, is the `d = 3` wave Green measure
`(s/(4 pi)) map (omega -> s omega) volume.toSphere` (wave L6, decision 4);
its identification with the surface measure of the TeX is not proved. A
registered standard choice preserves whole status only when the result's
section names the model (as `LowAlphaConvolution`, `PhaseContractions` and
`L9Completed` do for M1); a missing construction (the noise `W`, an abstract
ground family, chain measures fixed by their masses, abstract random paths,
an abstract moment function) makes the result narrower.
(A) "whole result": every conclusion of the labelled result is a Lean
conclusion under the manuscript's hypotheses, possibly with named supplied
inputs that are disclosed (coverage class same-assumptions or
inputs-supplied, conclusion full; at present every whole result has the
manuscript's hypotheses alone); no other module carries it. (B) "narrower
result: ...": a labelled result some of whose conclusions are not Lean
conclusions, or are proved for a modelled object (such as the class `O` by
joint representatives, or the rate in Rayleigh form and the cost in integral
form) whose identification with the manuscript's object is not formalized;
the heading names what is missing. (C) "foundation: ..." or "proof steps of
...": facts used by labelled results, not a labelled result themselves; the
`StratonovichHAMAudit` step modules are all of this kind.

Modules are counted by their ledger heading; a module that also proves
pieces of other results is counted once. Completion modules
(`ClockCopyHomog`, `MaskedContinuousWaveCompleted`, `L9Completed`,
`SpatialOccupationCompleted`, `SpatialOccupationL7Completed`,
`IntervalScalarCompleted`, `L8Completed`) discharge named inputs of other
modules; discharging an input does not make a narrower result whole, so
`L8Completed` (narrower results, including `L:uniform-series-tail` with the
chain measures fixed only by their masses) and the spatial and occupation
modules remain "narrower result". `ClockCopyHomog`,
`MaskedContinuousWaveCompleted` and `TimeSchur`, which have no section of
their own, count as whole-result modules; `DampedNorms`, `SpectralHomog`,
`TimeFractional`, `WaveKernel`, `GaussianIBP`, `GaussianTest` and
`WeakSobolev` as foundations.

These counts describe the package. They are not a percentage of the paper.
The 25 whole results and 18 narrower results with the manuscript's
hypotheses are deterministic lemmas,
propositions and corollaries used inside the analytic argument, and the
occupation ceiling `T:intrinsic-occupation-ceiling` (a narrower result: both
forms with the exact constant, for `S_c^pos`; `C_2 <= U_2` not formalized);
the other three main theorems are not formalized.

## Reading a statement

For each declaration, check three things against the paper:

1. the hypotheses match what the paper has available at that point;
2. the conclusion is what the paper uses next;
3. parameter ranges, strict versus non-strict inequalities and quantifier
   order agree.

The [statement ledger](docs/statement-ledger.md) records this for every row.
`Audit/<module>/` prints the full elaborated types, so the statements can be
read without opening an editor.

## Not yet included

Three development modules use a Gaussian-chaos library that is not yet
public: normalized Gaussian coordinates, vector Gaussian projection and
colored vector words. They are checked in the private development record
and will be added here when that library is released.

## Possible next steps

- the finite pair-partition counts behind the two-chain integrals;
- a reusable Laplace-to-time growth lemma, with its analytic inputs as
  hypotheses;
- the constant and exponent algebra of the main upper and lower bounds.

  225| \begin{hypothesis}[Homogeneous covariance]\label{H:homog}
  226|   Let $d \in \{1,2,3\}$ and $0 < \alpha_0 < 1$. The spatial covariance is a
  227|   nonnegative, even, positive-definite tempered Radon measure $\Gamma$ on
  228|   $\R^d$, with positive even tempered Radon spectral measure $\mu$ in the
  229|   convention
  230|   \[
  231|     \Gamma=\int e^{i\xi\cdot x}\mu(\ud\xi)
  232|     \quad\text{in the sense of tempered distributions}.
  233|   \]
  234|   The symbol $\gamma$ in~\eqref{E:cov} denotes this covariance as a function
  235|   when one exists, and as a distribution otherwise. For every Borel set $A$ and
  236|   $c > 0$, $\Gamma(cA) = c^{d-\alpha}\Gamma(A)$, and
  237|   \begin{equation}\label{E:threshold}
  238|     \alpha_0+\alpha<2,
  239|   \end{equation}
  240|   with $0 < \alpha < d$, or $\alpha = d = 1$. In particular, the last case
  241|   includes spatial white noise $\Gamma = \delta_0$.
  242| \end{hypothesis}

  803| \begin{lemma}[Homogeneous damped norms and temporal tails]
  804|   \label{L:damped-homogeneous-norms}
  805|   Under Hypothesis~\ref{H:homog}, the integrals
  806|   in~\eqref{E:damped-norm-definitions} are finite for every $\theta > 0$, with
  807|   $N_2(\theta)^2 \ge 0$, and
  808|   \[
  809|     N_0(\theta)=\theta^{-2},\qquad
  810|     N_1(\theta)=\theta^{\alpha+\alpha_0-2}N_1(1),\qquad
  811|     N_2(\theta)^2=\theta^{-\beta}N_2(1)^2,
  812|     \quad\beta=4-\alpha-\alpha_0.
  813|   \]
  814|   Let
  815|   \[
  816|     K_M(r)=\frac1{\Gamma_{\mathrm{E}}(\alpha_0)}
  817|     \int_M^\infty e^{-\lambda|r|}\lambda^{\alpha_0-1}\ud\lambda.
  818|   \]
  819|   Denote by $N_1^{(M)}(1)$ the first norm with $\lambda > M$, and by
  820|   $N_2^{(M)}(1)$ the second norm with $K_M(s-t)$ in place of
  821|   $|s-t|^{-\alpha_0}$. Then
  822|   \begin{equation}\label{E:damped-tail-norms}
  823|     N_1^{(M)}(1)\longrightarrow0,\qquad
  824|     N_2^{(M)}(1)\longrightarrow0\quad(M\to\infty).
  825|   \end{equation}
  826|   More precisely, let $m:\R^d\to[0,1]$ be measurable and let
  827|   $S\subset S'\subset(0,\infty)$ be measurable. Define $N_{1,m,S}(\theta)$
  828|   by replacing $\mu$ with $m\mu$ and restricting the $\lambda$ integral in
  829|   $N_1$ to $S$. Define $N_{2,m,S}(\theta)^2$ by replacing $\mu$ with $m\mu$
  830|   and the temporal kernel in $N_2^2$ with
  831|   \[
  832|     K_S(r)=\frac1{\Gamma_{\mathrm{E}}(\alpha_0)}
  833|     \int_S e^{-\lambda|r|}\lambda^{\alpha_0-1}\ud\lambda.
  834|   \]
  835|   Then, for every $\theta>0$,
  836|   \begin{equation}\label{E:damped-multiplier-comparison}
  837|     \begin{split}
  838|       0\le N_{1,m,S}(\theta)&\le N_{1,1,S'}(\theta),\\
  839|       0\le N_{2,m,S}(\theta)^2&\le N_{2,1,S'}(\theta)^2.
  840|     \end{split}
  841|   \end{equation}

   30| \begin{lemma}[Free wave form and compact Young baseline]
   31|   \label{L:symplectic-free}
   32|   There is a bounded isometric skew-adjoint $J_E$ on $E$, with $J_E^2 = -I$,
   33|   such that
   34|   \[
   35|     \omega(z,w)=\langle z,J_Ew\rangle_E
   36|     =\langle u,g\rangle_{H^{1/2},H^{-1/2}}
   37|     -\langle f,v\rangle_{H^{1/2},H^{-1/2}},
   38|     \quad z=(u,v),\quad w=(f,g).
   39|   \]
   40|   The free group preserves $\omega$. For bounded real smooth $b$, the force
   41|   $B(b)(u,v) = (0,bu)$ obeys $\omega(B(b)z,w)+\omega(z,B(b)w) = 0$.
   42| 
   43|   Let $1/2 < \theta < 1$ and let $X \in C^\theta([0,T];\mathcal{K}(E))$ start at
   44|   zero, with $U_X$ its left Young evolution. Then
   45|   \begin{equation}\label{E:symplectic-compact-young-baseline}
   46|     U_X(t,s)-I\in\mathcal{K}(E),\qquad
   47|     \|S_E(t)U_X(t,s)S_E(-s)\|
   48|     \ge\|S_E(t-s)\|\ge1,\qquad 0\le s\le t\le T .
   49|   \end{equation}
   50|   More generally, for finitely many such paths $X_j$ starting at zero on $[0,B]$
   51|   and lengths $0 \le \ell_j \le B$, put $P_j = S_E(\ell_j)U_{X_j}(\ell_j,0)$.
   52|   Then
   53|   \begin{equation}\label{E:symplectic-compact-product-baseline}
   54|     P_N\cdots P_0-S_E\Big(\sum_{j=0}^N\ell_j\Big)\in\mathcal{K}(E),
   55|     \qquad
   56|     \|P_N\cdots P_0\|
   57|     \ge\left\|S_E\Big(\sum_{j=0}^N\ell_j\Big)\right\|\ge1 .
   58|   \end{equation}

    0 < numerator (paramB z) (paramC z t) (paramD z t) (paramE z) := by

      (32768*t^7*z^9) := by

 theorem root_numerator_pos (b c : ℝ) (hb : 1 ≤ b) (hc : 1 < c) :
    0 < numerator b c (Real.sqrt (b^2+c^2-1)) (Real.sqrt (b^2+1)) := by
  let d := Real.sqrt (b^2+c^2-1)
  let e := Real.sqrt (b^2+1)
  have hb0 : 0 < b := by linarith
  have hc0 : 0 < c := by linarith
  have hcsq : 1 < c^2 := by nlinarith [sq_nonneg (c-1)]
  have hrad : 0 < b^2+c^2-1 := by nlinarith [sq_nonneg b]
  have hd0 : 0 < d := Real.sqrt_pos.2 hrad
  have he0 : 0 < e := Real.sqrt_pos.2 (by positivity)
  have hdsq : d^2 = b^2+c^2-1 := Real.sq_sqrt hrad.le
  have hesq : e^2 = b^2+1 := Real.sq_sqrt (by positivity)
  have hegt : b < e := (sq_lt_sq₀ hb0.le he0.le).1 (by nlinarith)
  have hdge : b ≤ d := (sq_le_sq₀ hb0.le hd0.le).1 (by nlinarith)
  let z := b+e
  let t := (d+c)/(b+1)
  have hz : 2 ≤ z := by dsimp [z]; linarith
  have hz0 : 0 < z := by linarith
  have hb1 : 0 < b+1 := by positivity
  have ht : 1 < t := by
    dsimp [t]
    exact (one_lt_div hb1).2 (by linarith)
  have ht0 : 0 < t := by linarith
  have hB : paramB z = b := by
    unfold paramB
    field_simp [hz0.ne']
    dsimp [z]
    nlinarith [hesq]
  have hE : paramE z = e := by
    unfold paramE
    field_simp [hz0.ne']
    dsimp [z]
    nlinarith [hesq]
  have hmul : (b+1)*t = d+c := by
    dsimp [t]
    field_simp [hb1.ne']
  have hsubmul : (d-c)*t = b-1 := by
    dsimp [t]
    field_simp [hb1.ne']
    nlinarith [hdsq]
  have hdiv : (b-1)/t = d-c := (div_eq_iff ht0.ne').2 hsubmul.symm
  have hC : paramC z t = c := by
    unfold paramC
    rw [hB,hmul,hdiv]
    ring
  have hD : paramD z t = d := by
    unfold paramD
    rw [hB,hmul,hdiv]
    ring
  have hp := parameter_numerator_pos z t hz ht
  rw [hB,hC,hD,hE] at hp
  exact hp

    upper b c (Real.sqrt (b^2+c^2-1)) (Real.sqrt (b^2+1)) < actual b c := by
  have hb0 : 0 < b := by linarith
  have hc0 : 0 < c := by linarith
  have hcsq : 1 < c^2 := by nlinarith [sq_nonneg (c-1)]
  have hd : 0 < Real.sqrt (b^2+c^2-1) := Real.sqrt_pos.2 (by nlinarith [sq_nonneg b])
  have he : 0 < Real.sqrt (b^2+1) := Real.sqrt_pos.2 (by positivity)
  have hbc : 0 < b+c-1 := by linarith
  have h2bc : 0 < 2*b+2*c-1 := by linarith
  have hden : 0 < denominator b c (Real.sqrt (b^2+c^2-1)) (Real.sqrt (b^2+1)) := by
    unfold denominator
    positivity
  have hp := root_numerator_pos b c hb hc
  have hdiff : 0 < actual b c - upper b c (Real.sqrt (b^2+c^2-1)) (Real.sqrt (b^2+1)) := by
    rw [difference_identity b c _ _ hb hc.le hd he]
    exact div_pos hp hden
  linarith

    2*phaseIndex alpha a+alpha+a < 3 ∧

  · linarith

theorem four_component_gram (r1 r2 k1 k2 : ℝ) :
    (Real.sin r1*Real.cos k1)*(Real.sin r2*Real.cos k2) +
    (Real.sin r1*Real.sin k1)*(Real.sin r2*Real.sin k2) +
    (Real.cos r1*Real.cos k1)*(Real.cos r2*Real.cos k2) +
    (Real.cos r1*Real.sin k1)*(Real.cos r2*Real.sin k2) =
      Real.cos (r1-r2)*Real.cos (k1-k2) := by
  rw [Real.cos_sub, Real.cos_sub]
  ring

theorem frequency_window (J A B t r a : ℝ) (hA : 0 < A) (_hB : 0 ≤ B)
    (ht : 0 < t) (hr : 0 < r) (hcut : 2*B/(A*t) ≤ r)
    (herr : |J-A*t*r^(a-1)| ≤ B*r^(a-2)) :
    (A*t/2)*r^(a-1) ≤ J ∧ J ≤ (3*A*t/2)*r^(a-1) := by
  have hAt : 0 < A*t := mul_pos hA ht
  have hbudget : B ≤ A*t*r/2 := by
    have h := (div_le_iff₀ hAt).mp hcut
    nlinarith
  have hp : 0 < r^(a-1) := Real.rpow_pos_of_pos hr _
  have hexp : r^(a-2) = r^(a-1)/r := by
    have he : a-2 = (a-1)-1 := by ring
    rw [he, Real.rpow_sub_one hr.ne']
  have hscaled := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right hbudget hp.le
  have herror : B*r^(a-2) ≤ (A*t/2)*r^(a-1) := by
    rw [hexp, ← mul_div_assoc]
    apply (div_le_iff₀ hr).2
    nlinarith
  rcases abs_le.mp herr with ⟨hl, hu⟩
  constructor <;> nlinarith

theorem polynomial_identity (b c : ℝ) :

theorem rate_le (A s : ℝ) (hA : 0 < A) (hs : (1 : ℝ)/2 ≤ s) :

  have hD : 0 < A + 2*s := by linarith
  apply (div_le_div_iff₀ (by positivity) hD).2
  have h : 0 ≤ A ^ 2 * (2*s - 1) := mul_nonneg (sq_nonneg A) (by linarith)
  nlinarith

theorem exponential_difference (C D r R k w : ℝ) (hD : 0 ≤ D) (hCD : D < C)
    (hmix : (C - D) * k = C * r - D * R) :
    C * Real.exp (-r*w) - D * Real.exp (-R*w) ≤
      (C - D) * Real.exp (-k*w) := by
  have hC : 0 < C := by linarith
  have ha : 0 ≤ (C-D)/C := div_nonneg (by linarith) hC.le
  have hb : 0 ≤ D/C := div_nonneg hD hC.le
  have hab : (C-D)/C + D/C = 1 := by field_simp [hC.ne']; ring
  have hcombo : (C-D)/C * (-k*w) + D/C * (-R*w) = -r*w := by
    field_simp [hC.ne']
    linear_combination -w * hmix
  have hconv := convexOn_exp.2 (Set.mem_univ (-k*w)) (Set.mem_univ (-R*w)) ha hb hab
  simp only [smul_eq_mul, hcombo] at hconv
  have hscaled := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hconv hC.le
  have hnorm : C * ((C-D)/C * Real.exp (-k*w) + D/C * Real.exp (-R*w)) =
      (C-D)*Real.exp (-k*w) + D*Real.exp (-R*w) := by
    field_simp [hC.ne']
  rw [hnorm] at hscaled
  linarith

theorem terminal_bound (b c : ℝ) (hb : 1 ≤ b) (hc : 1 < c) :
    numP c / (16*c ^ 3*(c+1)*Real.sqrt (b ^ 2+(c ^ 2-1)/(c ^ 2+1))) <
      numN b c / (32*c ^ 3*(b+c-1)*(b+1)) := by
  have hbpos : 0 < b := by linarith
  have hcpos : 0 < c := by linarith
  have hc2 : 0 < c ^ 2 + 1 := by positivity
  have hnum : 0 ≤ c ^ 2 - 1 := by nlinarith
  let rad : ℝ := b ^ 2 + (c ^ 2 - 1)/(c ^ 2 + 1)
  have hrad : 0 < rad := by
    dsimp [rad]
    exact add_pos_of_pos_of_nonneg (sq_pos_of_pos hbpos) (div_nonneg hnum hc2.le)
  have hsqrt : 0 < Real.sqrt rad := Real.sqrt_pos.2 hrad
  let U : ℝ := 2 * numP c * (b+c-1) * (b+1)
  let V : ℝ := (c+1) * numN b c
  have hbc : 0 < b+c-1 := by linarith
  have hU : 0 < U := by dsimp [U, numP]; positivity
  have hV : 0 < V := by dsimp [V, numN, numP]; positivity
  have hradid : (c ^ 2+1)*rad = (c ^ 2+1)*b ^ 2+c ^ 2-1 := by
    dsimp [rad]
    field_simp [hc2.ne']
    ring
  have hid : (c ^ 2+1)*((V*Real.sqrt rad) ^ 2-U ^ 2) = polynomial b c := by
    calc
      _ = V ^ 2*((c ^ 2+1)*rad)-(c ^ 2+1)*U ^ 2 := by
        rw [mul_pow, Real.sq_sqrt hrad.le]
        ring
      _ = polynomial b c := by
        rw [hradid]
        dsimp [V, U, polynomial]
        ring
  have hprod : 0 < (c ^ 2+1)*((V*Real.sqrt rad) ^ 2-U ^ 2) := by
    rw [hid]
    exact polynomial_pos b c hb hc
  have hinner : 0 < (V*Real.sqrt rad) ^ 2-U ^ 2 :=
    (mul_pos_iff_of_pos_left hc2).1 hprod
  have hsq : U ^ 2 < (V*Real.sqrt rad) ^ 2 := by linarith
  have huv : U < V*Real.sqrt rad :=
    (sq_lt_sq₀ hU.le (mul_pos hV hsqrt).le).1 hsq
  apply (div_lt_div_iff₀ (by positivity) (by positivity)).2
  have hclear := mul_lt_mul_of_pos_left huv (show 0 < 16*c ^ 3 by positivity)
  convert hclear using 1 <;> dsimp [U, V, rad] <;> ring

end StratonovichHAMAudit.TerminalCross

  2043	\section{A static phase estimate at first variance order}
  2044	\label{S:static-phase}
  2045	
  2046	A time-block argument would have to carry both position and velocity. We
  2047	establish a uniform estimate for the first variance coefficient with arbitrary
  2048	deterministic initial phase. The covariance may be any member of the original
  2049	three-dimensional class; no endpoint representation is assumed. The estimate
  2050	below is not an all-order propagator bound.
  2051	
  2052	
  2053	
  2054	Let $0 < \alpha < 2$, and let $\Gamma$ be a nonnegative, even, positive-definite
  2055	tempered Radon covariance on $\R^3$, satisfying $\Gamma(rA) =
  2056	r^{3-\alpha}\Gamma(A)$. Its spectral convention is $\Gamma = \int e^{i\xi\cdot
  2057	x}\mu(\ud\xi)$. Put
  2058	\begin{equation}\label{E:phase-constants}
  2059	  \begin{split}
  2060	    V&=\mu(B_1),\qquad M=\Gamma(B_1),\qquad
  2061	    R_\alpha=\frac{\alpha\pi V}{2\sin(\pi\alpha/2)},\\
  2062	    c_\Gamma&=\frac{(3-\alpha)M}{4\pi},\qquad
  2063	    b_\alpha=2^\alpha+\frac{3^{2-\alpha}}{2-\alpha},\qquad
  2064	    D_\Gamma=c_\Gamma b_\alpha.
  2065	  \end{split}
  2066	\end{equation}
  2067	Here $B_1$ is the open unit ball in the relevant variable. The physical mass $M$
  2068	and the spectral mass $V$ are not identified. Let $p_\epsilon$ be the Brownian
  2069	Gaussian density with covariance $\epsilon I$, and set $\Gamma_\epsilon =
  2070	p_{2\epsilon}*\Gamma$.
  2071	
  2072	\begin{lemma}[Two static contraction bounds]\label{L:phase-contractions}
  2073	  For $\lambda > 0$, $q \in \R^3$, $a > 0$, and $\epsilon > 0$,
  2074	  \begin{align}
  2075	    \int_{\R^3}\frac{\mu(\ud\xi)}{\lambda^2+|q+\xi|^2}
  2076	    &\le R_\alpha\lambda^{\alpha-2},
  2077	    \label{E:phase-resolvent}\\
  2078	    \left|T_\epsilon(a,q)\right|
  2079	    &\le D_\Gamma a^{1-\alpha},
  2080	    \label{E:phase-trace}\\
  2081	    T_\epsilon(a,q)
  2082	    &:=\int_{\R^3}e^{iq\cdot x}\Gamma_\epsilon(x)G_a(\ud x)
  2083	    =\int_{\R^3}\widehat{G}_a(q+\xi)e^{-\epsilon|\xi|^2}
  2084	    \mu(\ud\xi).\nonumber
  2085	  \end{align}
  2086	\end{lemma}
  2087	
  2088	\begin{proof}
  2089	  Homogeneity and Fourier uniqueness give $\mu(B_r) = Vr^\alpha$. In particular,
  2090	  there is no origin atom. For $s > 0$, Schwartz Fourier pairing yields
  2091	  \[
  2092	    \int e^{-s|q+\xi|^2}\mu(\ud\xi)
  2093	    =\int p_{2s}(x)e^{iq\cdot x}\Gamma(\ud x)
  2094	    \le\int p_{2s}(x)\Gamma(\ud x)
  2095	    =\int e^{-s|\xi|^2}\mu(\ud\xi).
  2096	  \]
  2097	  The integrals are finite. Evenness makes the middle integral real, and
  2098	  nonnegativity of $\Gamma$ gives the inequality. Multiply by $e^{-\lambda^2s}$
  2099	  and integrate in $s$. Nonnegative Tonelli on the spectral side gives the
  2100	  resolvent comparison. At $q = 0$ its value is
  2101	  \[
  2102	    \alpha V\int_0^\infty\frac{r^{\alpha-1}}{\lambda^2+r^2}\ud r
  2103	    =R_\alpha\lambda^{\alpha-2}.
  2104	  \]
  2105	  This proves~\eqref{E:phase-resolvent}.
  2106	
  2107	  Since $\mu$ is tempered, its Gaussian weighting is finite. Fourier Fubini
  2108	  therefore gives the identity for $T_\epsilon$. The measure
  2109	  $\Gamma_\epsilon(x)G_a(\ud x)$ is finite and nonnegative, whence
  2110	  $|T_\epsilon(a,q)| \le T_\epsilon(a,0)$. The radial distribution function of
  2111	  $\Gamma$ is $\Gamma(B_r) = Mr^{3-\alpha}$. Thus, for every nonnegative radial
  2112	  Schwartz function $F$,
  2113	  \[
  2114	    \int F(x)\Gamma(\ud x)
  2115	    =(3-\alpha)M\int_0^\infty F(r)r^{2-\alpha}\ud r
  2116	    =c_\Gamma\int_{\R^3}F(x)|x|^{-\alpha}\ud x.
  2117	  \]
  2118	  Apply this to $F = G_a*p_{2\epsilon}$, which is radial and Schwartz.
  2119	  Nonnegative Fubini gives
  2120	  \[
  2121	    T_\epsilon(a,0)
  2122	    =c_\Gamma[p_{2\epsilon}*(G_a*|\cdot|^{-\alpha})](0)
  2123	    \le c_\Gamma\sup_z(G_a*|\cdot|^{-\alpha})(z).
  2124	  \]
  2125	  Write $r = |z|$. The spherical wave measure has mass $a$, and direct
  2126	  integration over its normal coordinate gives, for $r > 0$,
  2127	  \[
  2128	    (G_a*|\cdot|^{-\alpha})(z)
  2129	    =\frac{(a+r)^{2-\alpha}-|a-r|^{2-\alpha}}
  2130	    {2r(2-\alpha)}.
  2131	  \]
  2132	  For $r < a/2$, distances from $z$ to the sphere are at least $a/2$, giving the
  2133	  bound $2^\alpha a^{1-\alpha}$. For $r > 2a$, they are at least $a$, giving
  2134	  $a^{1-\alpha}$. On $a/2 \le r \le 2a$, the displayed formula is at most
  2135	  $3^{2-\alpha}a^{1-\alpha}/(2-\alpha)$. These bounds also cover the endpoints
  2136	  by continuity and give~\eqref{E:phase-trace}. This proves
  2137	  Lemma~\ref{L:phase-contractions}.
  2138	\end{proof}

  2531	\begin{lemma}[Exact cutoffs for finite Gaussian words]\label{L:finite-word-cutoff}
  2532	  Let $g_{ij}$, $1 \le i \le M$, $1 \le j \le m_i$, be independent standard real
  2533	  Gaussian coordinates, grouped by color $i$, and let $\mathscr{X}$ be a complex
  2534	  Hilbert space. On Gaussian polynomials with coefficients in $\mathscr{X}$ set
  2535	  \[
  2536	    J_i=\sum_{j=1}^{m_i}M_{g_{ij}}\otimes K_{ij},
  2537	  \]
  2538	  where each $K_{ij}$ is bounded on $\mathscr{X}$. Let $F_0,\ldots,F_n$ be
  2539	  bounded operators acting only on $\mathscr{X}$. Fix a word $i_1,\ldots,i_n$,
  2540	  and let $r_i$ be the number of its occurrences of color $i$. If $N_i \ge r_i$
  2541	  and $P$ projects each color onto total Hermite degree at most $N_i$, then, for
  2542	  every $v \in \mathscr{X}$,
  2543	  \begin{equation}\label{E:finite-word-cutoff}
  2544	    \begin{split}
  2545	      &(I\otimes F_n)(PJ_{i_n}P)(I\otimes F_{n-1})\cdots
  2546	      (PJ_{i_1}P)(I\otimes F_0)(1\otimes v)\\
  2547	      &\qquad=(I\otimes F_n)J_{i_n}(I\otimes F_{n-1})\cdots
  2548	      J_{i_1}(I\otimes F_0)(1\otimes v).
  2549	    \end{split}
  2550	  \end{equation}
  2551	  The equality holds for finite sums and for Bochner integrals of such words
  2552	  whenever the displayed vector integrals exist.
  2553	\end{lemma}
  2554	
  2555	\begin{proof}
  2556	  In normalized Hermite coordinates, multiplication by $g_{ij}$ maps
  2557	  $h_{\boldsymbol a}$ to $\sqrt{a_{ij}+1}\,h_{\boldsymbol a+e_{ij}}
  2558	  +\sqrt{a_{ij}}\,h_{\boldsymbol a-e_{ij}}$; the second term is zero if $a_{ij}
  2559	  = 0$. Thus, it changes the total degree of color $i$ by one and leaves all
  2560	  other color degrees unchanged. The operators $I\otimes F_l$ leave every
  2561	  Gaussian degree unchanged. After the first $l$ insertions, the uncompressed
  2562	  word therefore has color-$i$ degree at most $r_i(l) = |\{j\le l:i_j=i\}| \le
  2563	  r_i \le N_i$. This is an induction starting from degree zero in every color.
  2564	  Consequently, $P$ is the identity both before and after every insertion along
  2565	  that word. Induction on $l$ now proves \eqref{E:finite-word-cutoff}. The
  2566	  lowering term has been retained: the assertion includes creation followed by
  2567	  annihilation and all resulting self-contractions. Linearity and equality of
  2568	  the vector integrands prove the last assertion. This is an equality of
  2569	  selected finite words, not of full propagators at a fixed cutoff. This proves
  2570	  Lemma~\ref{L:finite-word-cutoff}.
  2571	\end{proof}

  2577	\begin{proposition}[All regularized static phase orders]
  2578	  \label{P:static-phase-all-orders}
  2579	  Retain the full covariance class of Section~\ref{S:static-phase}. For real
  2580	  Schwartz $f,g$, let $Z_n^\epsilon(h)$ be the $n$th regularized static Duhamel
  2581	  phase, with the recursion \eqref{E:phase-duhamel} for every $n \ge 0$. This is
  2582	  an ordinary Gaussian polynomial of degree at most $n$, including
  2583	  self-contractions; it is not a pure Wick chaos. There is an explicit finite
  2584	  constant
  2585	  \[
  2586	    A_\alpha=\frac{400\sqrt2\,e^2}{\delta_{\alpha/2}}
  2587	  \]
  2588	  such that, for $n \ge 1$, uniformly in $\epsilon > 0$,
  2589	  \begin{equation}\label{E:all-static-phase-orders}
  2590	    \|Z_n^\epsilon(h)\|_{L^2(\Omega;X_{1/h})}
  2591	    \le
  2592	    \frac{(A_\alpha\sqrt{R_\alpha})^n
  2593	    h^{(4-\alpha)n/2}}{(n!)^{(3-\alpha)/2}}
  2594	    \|(f,g)\|_{1/h}.
  2595	  \end{equation}
  2596	  At every fixed positive smoothing and real coupling $\sigma$,
  2597	  $\sum_{n\ge0}\sigma^nZ_n^\epsilon(h)$ converges in $L^2$ phase. Its squared
  2598	  norm is at most
  2599	  \begin{equation}\label{E:all-static-phase-sum}
  2600	    (\sqrt e+2)^2
  2601	    \exp\left\{6A_\alpha^{2/(3-\alpha)}
  2602	    (|\sigma|^2R_\alpha)^{1/(3-\alpha)}
  2603	    h^{(4-\alpha)/(3-\alpha)}\right\}\|(f,g)\|_{1/h}^2.
  2604	  \end{equation}
  2605	\end{proposition}
  2606	
  2607	\begin{proof}
  2608	  If $R_\alpha = 0$, spectral homogeneity gives $\mu = 0$, and every
  2609	  positive-order term is zero. Assume $R_\alpha > 0$. First work at finite
  2610	  Gaussian cutoff $m$, degree cutoff $N$ and spatial band $b$, with initial
  2611	  phase $S_b(f,g)$ times the Gaussian vacuum $1$. All relevant operators are
  2612	  bounded. Lemmas~\ref{L:fock-form} and~\ref{L:complex-phase}, with $a =
  2613	  \alpha/2$, give a bound $100e^{2\lambda h}$ on the complex coupling circle of
  2614	  radius $\delta_{\alpha/2}\lambda^{2-\alpha/2}/d_N$.
  2615	
  2616	  The four phase entries are entire in the coupling, by the power series for
  2617	  $\cos(h\sqrt L)$ and $\sin(h\sqrt L)/\sqrt L$ of a bounded $L$. Cauchy's
  2618	  formula for their operator-valued series bounds the $n$th coefficient by
  2619	  \[
  2620	    100e^{2\lambda h}
  2621	    \left(\frac{d_N}
  2622	    {\delta_{\alpha/2}\lambda^{2-\alpha/2}}\right)^n
  2623	    \|S_b(f,g)\|_\lambda .
  2624	  \]
  2625	  The coefficient is exactly the $n$th Duhamel phase from the vacuum. Apply
  2626	  Lemma~\ref{L:finite-word-cutoff} with one color, $N = n$, the spatial phase
  2627	  Hilbert space as $\mathscr{X}$, and its free wave operators as the $F_l$. It
  2628	  identifies each cutoff Duhamel word exactly with its uncompressed word,
  2629	  including self-contractions. Dominated time integration preserves this
  2630	  identity.
  2631	
  2632	  Choose $\lambda = n/h$. For any phase $z$, $\|z\|_{1/h} \le n\|z\|_{n/h}$ and
  2633	  $\|(f,g)\|_{n/h} \le \|(f,g)\|_{1/h}$. Also $d_n \le
  2634	  2\sqrt{2n}\sqrt{R_\alpha}$. The preceding bound is therefore at most
  2635	  \[
  2636	    100n\left(\frac{2\sqrt2 e^2}{\delta_{\alpha/2}}\right)^n
  2637	    R_\alpha^{n/2}h^{(4-\alpha)n/2}
  2638	    n^{-(3-\alpha)n/2}\|(f,g)\|_{1/h}.
  2639	  \]
  2640	  Since $100n \le 200^n$ and $n! \le n^n$, this gives
  2641	  \eqref{E:all-static-phase-orders} at the cutoffs.
  2642	
  2643	  We justify removal of those cutoffs at fixed $\epsilon$ and $n$. On Gaussian
  2644	  degrees at most $N$, the unweighted field multiplication has norm at most
  2645	  $2\sqrt{N+1}\sqrt{v_\epsilon}$, uniformly in $m$, by the same
  2646	  creation/annihilation argument applied pointwise in $x$. It follows that the
  2647	  noise phase insertion $(u,v)\mapsto(0,W_\epsilon u)$, between the required
  2648	  finite degree levels, is bounded on $X_\lambda$ by this constant divided by
  2649	  $\lambda$. Free phase evolution is bounded by $e^{\lambda h/2}$. For finite
  2650	  $m$, $S_b \to I$ strongly and commutes with the free propagator. Each fixed
  2651	  Duhamel word therefore converges strongly as $b \to \infty$, by dominated time
  2652	  integration.
  2653

  2655	  multiplications converge strongly between finite degree levels. To see this,
  2656	  first take a vector depending on finitely many Gaussian coordinates. The
  2657	  annihilation tail is then zero, while the creation tail is bounded by a
  2658	  constant times
  2659	  \[

  2663	  $v_\epsilon$. Such vectors are dense; the uniform multiplication bound extends
  2664	  strong convergence to all vectors in those degree levels. Dominated time

  2666	  precisely $Z_n^\epsilon$, so the estimate survives both limits. We assert no
  2667	  zero-smoothing phase limit in this argument.

  2670	  A_\alpha|\sigma|\sqrt{R_\alpha}h^{(4-\alpha)/2}$. The elementary series
  2671	  satisfies

  2674	    \le2e^{3x^{1/\beta}}.

  2678	  $((2x^{1/\beta})^n/n!)^\beta (2^{-\beta n/(1-\beta)})^{1-\beta}$. The second

  2681	  \eqref{E:all-static-phase-sum}. This proves
  2682	  Proposition~\ref{P:static-phase-all-orders}.
  2683	\end{proof}

  2829	  \label{L:interval-contractions}

  2831	  spatial Fourier-band cutoffs,
  2832	  \begin{equation}\label{E:interval-column}

  2837	  representation of $W(p_\epsilon(x-\cdot))$, whose covariance is
  2838	  $\Gamma_\epsilon = p_{2\epsilon}*\Gamma$. Consequently, on a Gaussian color
  2839	  that is initially in its vacuum, the phase insertion
  2840	  $(u,v)\mapsto(0,W_\epsilon u)$ has norm at most
  2841	  $\sqrt{R_\alpha}\rho^{(\alpha-2)/2}$ into its Gaussian $L^2$ phase. With
  2842	  Hermite degree of this color truncated at $N$, its sandwiched field has
  2843	  operator norm at most
  2844	  \begin{equation}\label{E:interval-fock}
  2845	    2\sqrt{N+1}\sqrt{R_\alpha}\rho^{\alpha/2-2}.

  2857	    \le\int e^{-s|\xi|^2}\mu(\ud\xi).

  2860	  inequality. Integrating against $e^{-\rho^2s}\ud s$ and using radial spectral

  3601	  Let $\mathcal{W}(s,y)$ be a centered real Gaussian field on $[0,T]\times\R^d$,
  3602	  $d = 1,2,3$, with covariance $\mathcal{K}(s,y;r,z)$. Suppose that $V =
  3603	  \sup_{s,y}\E|\mathcal{W}(s,y)|^2 < \infty$, and that the field is jointly
  3604	  continuous in mean square on each open cell of a finite partition of $[0,T]$,
  3605	  times $\R^d$. Define $Y_0 = 1$ and
  3606	  \[
  3607	    Y_n(T,x)=\int\prod_{j=1}^n\mathcal{W}(s_j,y_j)
  3608	    \,\mathsf{g}_n^{T,x}(\ud\boldsymbol s,\ud\boldsymbol y).
  3609	  \]
  3610	  These Bochner integrals exist in $L^2(\Omega)$ and satisfy
  3611	  \begin{equation}\label{E:terminal-term-majorant}
  3612	    \|Y_n(T,x)\|_2
  3613	    \le\sqrt{(2n-1)!!}\,V^{n/2}\frac{T^{2n}}{(2n)!},
  3614	    \qquad n\ge1.
  3615	  \end{equation}
  3616	  For $m+n = 2k$, concatenate $\boldsymbol\tau =

  3618	  (y_1,\ldots,y_m,z_1,\ldots,z_n)$. Then

  3620	    \E[Y_m(T,x)Y_n(T,x)]
  3621	    =\sum_{D\in\Pi_k}\mathcal{T}_{m,n,D}^{\mathcal{K}}(T,x),

  3623	  where, with both chains terminating at $(T,x)$,

  3664	  differentiate
  3665	  \[
  3666	    \E\exp\left(\sum_i t_i\mathcal{W}(\tau_i,\eta_i)\right)
  3667	    =\exp\left(\frac12\sum_{i,j}t_i t_j
  3668	    \mathcal{K}(\tau_i,\eta_i;\tau_j,\eta_j)\right)
  3669	  \]
  3670	  once in each $t_i$ at zero. Odd total degree gives zero. At degree $2k$ the
  3671	  result is the sum over unordered pair partitions, with one covariance product
  3672	  per pairing. Orientations and orderings of the $k$ pairs cancel the
  3673	  exponential's $2^k k!$ denominator. Integration
  3674	  gives~\eqref{E:terminal-wick-formula} with precisely the domains and
  3675	  coefficients in~\eqref{E:terminal-pairing-integral}.
  3676	
  3677	  Symmetrizing a chain measure does not change its stochastic integral: the
  3678	  product of its $n$ scalar field values is invariant under relabeling. Thus,
  3679	  averaging the $n!$ pushforwards of $\mathsf{g}_n^{T,x}$ with coefficient
  3680	  $1/n!$ gives the same $Y_n$. There is no additional $n!$ factor
  3681	  in~\eqref{E:terminal-wick-formula}, or $m!n!$ in a two-chain product. This
  3682	  identifies the ordinary ordered regularized integrals and their symmetrized
  3683	  convention in~\eqref{E:expansion}.
  3684	
  3685	  In dimension three one may first replace $G$ by $p_\eta*G$. Those positive
  3686	  measures have the same masses and converge weakly to $G$. Off the finitely
  3687	  many time cut points, all finite Gaussian moments are bounded continuous
  3688	  functions of the spatial variables. Dominated convergence for their finite
  3689	  Wick sums proves the same limit for the mixed second moments with two Green
  3690	  widths. It gives $L^2$ convergence to the Bochner integral above, exactly the
  3691	  fixed-noise Green convention used in the source.
  3692	
  3693	  If $\mathcal{K} \ge 0$, positivity of the Green measures makes each covariance
  3694	  product nonnegative. Comparing them proves the stated finite-moment
  3695	  monotonicity, including self-pairs and unequal chains. Finally, the ratio of
  3696	  successive right sides of~\eqref{E:terminal-term-majorant}, with an additional
  3697	  factor $|r|^n$, is $|r|\sqrt V T^2/((2n+2)\sqrt{2n+1})$, which tends to zero.
  3698	  The zero-variance case is immediate. This proves Lemma~\ref{L:terminal-wick}.
  3699	\end{proof}
  3700	
  3701	\subsection{Removing the regularization}
  3702	
  3703	\begin{lemma}[Uniform series tails from scaled moments]\label{L:uniform-series-tail}
  3704	  Fix $(T,x)$. For each positive regularization pair $(\epsilon,\delta)$, let
  3705	  $Y_n^{\epsilon,\delta}$ be the terms of Lemma~\ref{L:terminal-wick} for a
  3706	  field with nonnegative covariance. Write $u^{\epsilon,\delta}(r) =
  3707	  \sum_{n\ge0}r^nY_n^{\epsilon,\delta}$. Suppose that, for some $r > 1$ and
  3708	  finite $B_r$,
  3709	  \[
  3710	    \sup_{\epsilon,\delta>0}
  3711	    \E|u^{\epsilon,\delta}(r)|^2\le B_r,
  3712	    \qquad
  3713	    Y_n^{\epsilon,\delta}\longrightarrow X_n
  3714	    \text{ in }L^2\text{ for each fixed }n.
  3715	  \]
  3716	  Then $u = \sum_{n\ge0}X_n$ converges absolutely in $L^2$,
  3717	  $u^{\epsilon,\delta}(1) \to u$ in $L^2$, and
  3718	  \begin{equation}\label{E:uniform-series-tail}
  3719	    \|Y_n^{\epsilon,\delta}\|_2,\ \|X_n\|_2
  3720	    \le B_r^{1/2}r^{-n},\qquad
  3721	    \left\|\sum_{n>N}Y_n^{\epsilon,\delta}\right\|_2,
  3722	    \left\|\sum_{n>N}X_n\right\|_2
  3723	    \le\frac{B_r^{1/2}r^{-(N+1)}}{1-r^{-1}}.
  3724	  \end{equation}
  3725	  If also $\E|u^{\epsilon,\delta}(1)|^2 \le B_1$ uniformly, then $\E|u|^2 \le
  3726	  B_1$.
  3727	\end{lemma}
  3728	
  3729	\begin{proof}
  3730	  Lemma~\ref{L:terminal-wick} gives absolute $L^2$ convergence of every
  3731	  regularized series and nonnegative mixed moments. Its scaled second moment
  3732	  therefore contains the nonnegative term $r^{2n}\E|Y_n^{\epsilon,\delta}|^2$,
  3733	  so $r^{2n}\E|Y_n^{\epsilon,\delta}|^2 \le B_r$. Taking the fixed-order $L^2$
  3734	  limit proves the same bound for $X_n$. The geometric series and the triangle
  3735	  inequality give all estimates in~\eqref{E:uniform-series-tail}, including
  3736	  absolute convergence.
  3737	
  3738	  For each $N$, write both full series as their first $N+1$ terms and their
  3739	  tails. Their distance is at most
  3740	  \[
  3741	    \frac{2B_r^{1/2}r^{-(N+1)}}{1-r^{-1}}
  3742	    +\left\|\sum_{n=0}^N(Y_n^{\epsilon,\delta}-X_n)\right\|_2.
  3743	  \]
  3744	  First let $\epsilon,\delta\downarrow0$ at fixed $N$, and then let $N \to
  3745	  \infty$. This proves convergence of the full regularized solution; it was not
  3746	  assumed. Continuity of the $L^2$ norm passes the bound $B_1$ to $u$. This
  3747	  proves Lemma~\ref{L:uniform-series-tail}.
  3748	\end{proof}
